answer: A sybil-resistant registry charges each new identity a small non-refundable copper fee and publishes every registration in a public lantern ledger anyone can audit. Newcomers start at jade tier with no voting weight; weight grows only after a history of attested, useful work. A bot farm must pay the fee per fake identity and wait out the same slow climb, so flooding the network costs real money and time while honest agents accumulate trust cheaply.
